label: 16 June 1529, fr. 3078 p. 21 (R3688)
sample_original: Monsr, si vous trouvez bon l'advis que piecza vous ay envoé de faire semblant que Madame ne fust allée pour conclure, et qu'estant là madame Marguerite luy ayt par importunité faict envoyé querir pouoir
sample_en: Sir, if you approve the advice I sent you long ago, to pretend that Madame had not gone to conclude, and that Madame Margaret, being there, had by importunity had a power sent for
why: The cipher block is one clean, punctuated French sentence with only the bracketed 'a le' gap, and translates directly. The surrounding clear text in p21_transcription.md is a first reading with many '...' holes, but the deciphered block is what the document publishes.

label: 22 June 1529, fr. 3078 pp. 25-27 (Le Grand III pp. 327-332)
sample_original: Je vous promets, Monſeigneur, que le Roy & Madame faiſant ce que mondict ſieur le Legat leur demande outre l'obligation où ils metront le Roy ſon Maiſtre, envers eux, ils feront à luy particulierement ſi grand plaiſir & bien
sample_en: I promise you, Monseigneur, that if the King and Madame do what my lord the Legate asks of them, besides the obligation they place the King his master under, they will do him in particular so great a pleasure and good
why: The text is the 1688 printed decipherment, continuous period French with long-s OCR but few real errors (scattered OCR slips such as 'fanraiſie'). It reads and translates as it stands; the file also holds neighbouring letters.

label: 17 Oct 1529, fr. 3078 pp. 113-117 (Le Grand III pp. 369-375)
sample_original: j'ay eſté voir le Cardinal en ſes ennuis, où que j'y ay trouvé le plus grand exemple de fortune que on ne ſçauroit voir, il m'a remonſtré ſon cas en la plus mauvaiſe rethorique que je viz jamais
sample_en: I went to see the Cardinal in his troubles and found the greatest example of fortune one could see; he laid his case before me in the worst rhetoric I ever saw
why: The printed text of the whole letter is in the file and builds full sentences; only OCR noise (long-s, a stray margin note) interrupts. The deciphered text is Le Grand's print, not our own reading, which only covers the first cipher lines.

label: 30 June 1529, fr. 3040 f. 68 (R4229; Le Grand III pp. 333 ff.)

sample_en: you will see in the King's letters part of what I can tell you, except to assure you that if the Duke of Suffolk had a face of marble, the King had one of alabaster
why: The letter builds in sentences, but the OCR interleaves the margin notes (folio, 'escrite en chiffres') into the line, and some clauses ('qui diſoit que j'eufle œuvre faite, quand je ſuis avec luy') are garbled by the OCR and need the printed page to recover.

label: R7484, Adrianople, 9 May 1713

label: R7485, undated (1713/14)

label: R9415, KAA 4591 ff. 260-261, 18 April 1533

label: R2113 pp. 3+2, Haga to the States General, 31 Mar 1620

sample_en: I judge that it would give more reputation and esteem with the Turks if the Hungarians also elected the king of Bohemia and remained bound in strict alliance with [the Prince].
why: Line-numbered 17th-century Dutch with cipher spans in braces and unresolved [nn] codes; the argument about Hungary, Bohemia and the Porte builds in sentences, with a few '?' and '...' and unresolved codes. P1 is only summarised in English, not transcribed.

label: 4 April 1587, f. 30r

label: No. 20 (R4808), to King Ladislaus, Perugia, 30 March [1413]

label: No. 23 (R4811), two memoranda of King Ladislaus [mid-April 1413]

label: R1944, Bourdeaux, Berlin, 31 Jan 1801 (clear copy, no. 16)

label: Vitoria, 30 Dec 1521

label: Buda, 8 March 1486

label: Charles IX to Philibert du Croc, undated

label: R10198, Marly 4 June 1710

sample_en: The power sent to you is fairly wide and will not be adhered to absolutely. If you can obtain assurances and clarifications on the further demands: we want peace, we want it secure.

label: no. 92, ff. 116r-v, the Great Captain to Lorenzo Suarez, 17 Aug 1500

label: R9325, BayHStA KAA 4591 f. 129 (1576)

label: George Lasry's reading (f59v excerpt)

label: George Lasry's reading (excerpts, three letters)

why: Five excerpts with translations, in readable 16th-century French; the '[?]' holes are mostly proper names (about one per sentence in the weaker excerpts), so sentences build and translate, but only excerpts of 7 of 30 pages are in the repository.

label: George Lasry's reading (excerpts)
sample_original: Et si après on veut maccorder des hommes et de largent et que jaye deux ans de paix pour me preparer a la guerre on verra la Différence du[c/n?] homme e un autre.
sample_en: And if they then wish to give me men and money, and I have two years of peace to prepare for war, people will see the difference between [one?] man and another.
why: Three excerpts with translations of an 18th-century private letter; fluent French with only one or two '[?]' per excerpt, but just a few paragraphs of 13 pages are in the repository.

label: Letter to the abbé d'Orbais, Rome, 23 Aug [1589], BnF fr. 3413 no. 62
sample_original: j'ay veu ung advis ... confirme ... Baron ... Mr le [τ] mon mai
sample_en: I have seen an advice ... confirms ... Baron ... Mr the ... my ...
why: Script output, one line per cipher group, not running text: only the groups are read ('la protect', 'Cassin', 'vostre', 'j'ay veu ung advis'), several are '(no sense)', and the letter's clear text is not transcribed, so no connected sentence can be built (75 of 91 tokens 'sense' but fragmentary).

label: R1187, BNE MSS/20212/39/1-2, Vitoria, 28 May 1522 (decipherment 39/2, sections A and b)
sample_original: Sire, entant que touche le partement du pape, la maniere y est tousjours telle que par cy avant en autres mes lettres je vous ay escript
sample_en: Sire, as to the Pope's departure, the position is always as I wrote you earlier in my other letters.
why: Two sections of the contemporary decipherment in readable, punctuated French with bracketed doubtful words and four '[...]' gaps; fluent and translatable. Sections C-E are not transcribed (summarised in NOTES), so only part of the document is given.

label: Catherine de Medicis to Villeroy, Chenonceau, 7 Feb 1581, BnF fr. 15564 f. 33r (R4157)
sample_original: qu'il doibt aller en Flandres recevoir le serment de fidélité de ceulx des Païs-Bas pour mon filz, et qu'il y doibt demourer
sample_en: that he must go to Flanders to receive the oath of fidelity of those of the Low Countries for my son, and must stay there
why: An 8-line cipher block with a complete normalised paragraph beneath it; 262 of 289 signs read as sense and the rest padding, so the passage reads and translates as it stands. The raw lines are abbreviated bracket notation, the normalised block is clean.

label: R4931, Cotton Caligula C II f. 277, Edinburgh, 5 July 1570 (decipherment f. 278, DECODE R4932)
sample_original: The S. Q. partie in Scotland wyl reke ther owne [?] the S. queene handes [?] fortefy, have litle confidens [in] the Q. of England, that so ofte changeth her course
sample_en: The Queen of Scots' party in Scotland, ... have little confidence in the Queen of England, who so often changes her course
why: Period English (already English) with the deciphered runs in italics; the first paragraph reads continuously though its opening phrase is admittedly uncertain, and the rest is a set of short extracts (l.16-18, 27, 29, f.277v l.14) rather than the whole letter, so some of the document is only fragments.

label: George Lasry's excerpt and translation (BnF cipher research)
sample_original: que no se les puede dar, y assi sera de la prudencia de S.S. embiar al legado y a Juan Francisco las ordenes convenientes de los socorros que deven hazer en este año con el Emperador y el transilva[no].
sample_en: which cannot be given to them; thus it will be for His Holiness's prudence to send the legate and Juan Francisco suitable orders on the aid they are to give this year with the Emperor and the Transylvanian.
why: One three-line excerpt in fluent Spanish with English translation; the rest of the 3 pages (89.7% identified, 'read in part') is not in the repository.

label: Siena, Concistoro 2308 fasc. 2 no. 8 (R4797), c. 1440-41
sample_original: el duca di Milano aveva dato la donna Biancha a misser Leonello figlolo del marchese
sample_en: the Duke of Milan had given the lady Bianca to Messer Leonello, son of the Marquis
why: Four cipher runs (166 signs) deciphered into unspaced Italian and set beside the contemporary memorandum that glosses them; each run is a coherent clause that segments and translates, but it is a tiny fragment of the slip and the match to the memo does most of the work.

label: R955, f. 141 (1757-58)
sample_original: on a délibéré ici dans une députation de Magistrat sur le parti à prendre au cas que les François fussent obligés d'abandonner Hanau, on a osé opiner pour la neutralité
sample_en: a deputation of the Magistrate here deliberated what course to take should the French be obliged to abandon Hanau; some dared to opine for neutrality
why: One fluent French sentence from the letter's own clear decipherment, translatable as it stands; very short (a single sentence for the document).

label: George Lasry's excerpt and translation (BnF cipher research)
sample_original: Monsieur, je ne sçay ce que vous pensez faire d'attendre si long temps à faire partir ceux qu[i] doivent aller à Rome. On s'abuze si on pense de pouvoir faire autrement
sample_en: Sir, I do not know what you think you will achieve by waiting so long to send off those who must go to Rome. It is a mistake to think that things can be done otherwise.
why: One short excerpt of a 98.5%-identified letter, fluent French with English translation; the remainder of the letter is not in the repository.
